A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, despite the changed title and FedRGB-to-FedAID renaming. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including v2's image-embedded pseudocode, which was inspected visually.

before.justification: V1 reports original federated pre-training experiments, downstream classification, segmentation and retrieval results, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports revised baseline comparisons in Table 1, with further empirical results throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: The top-level pseudocode moves the client-loss calculation used for DRO reweighting from before local updates in v1 Algorithm 1 to after local training in v2 Algorithm 1, lines 8-12. This revises the reported update sequence; the architecture, guidance and DRO losses, and two-stage design otherwise remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CXR with Chest imaGenome annotations, RSNA and Covid classification, RSNA segmentation, and EHRXQA-derived out-of-distribution retrieval. No additional dataset, domain, or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: The primary comparison changes substantially: v2 Table 1 adds FedMOON and ImageNet Init ViT while dropping FedX and the decentralized row from v1 Table 2. FedX is also removed from the out-of-distribution comparison. Decentralized comparisons remain elsewhere, including the GLoRIA/MGCA experiments.

E3.justification: The partition description changes from training/validation to training/test in Section 5.1 and the experiment details, although retrieval still refers to validation splits. V2 also explicitly counts additional client work and transmissions within a communication round. These are reported protocol changes; different actual splits or reruns are not established.

E4.justification: V1's comparative computation and communication overhead analysis, including Table 9, is removed. The alignment/guidance ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, convergence, distortion, client-count, and out-of-distribution analyses are otherwise retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Client-average, worst-client, and cross-client disparity reporting retain the same practices.

E6.justification: The main baseline results are substantially revised: FedMAE's Covid 1% accuracy changes from 42.25 to 77.50 and retrieval Recall@1 from 5.05 to 8.29. ImageNet and FedMOON results are added, while FedX and cost results are removed. The proposed method's main scores and GLoRIA/MGCA results remain unchanged. V2 Appendix Table 8 retains the older FedMAE retrieval values.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's probabilistic and DRO formulations, v2 introduces a Lipschitz-loss assumption, Remark 1 and its derivation in Appendix G.1, and an alignment-probability definition and bound in G.2. These substantially expand the formal mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain heterogeneous medical federated VLP, teacher-guided alignment with DRO, and improved transferability across retrieval, classification, and segmentation. The new title and alignment-binding terminology largely reframe these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds a rationale for keeping local aligners learnable while binding their representations. It revises the baseline interpretation to acknowledge visual transferability while emphasizing weaker cross-modal retrieval, replacing the specific FedX and masking explanations. The privacy and limited-modality limitations are retained in Appendix H.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies uniform initial client weights and adds MIMIC-CXR access instructions. It removes the stated gamma=1 setting and the parameter-count, training-time, FLOP, and communication-cost details from v1 Table 9. Hardware, batch size, learning rate, and preprocessing information remain.

R1.justification: Related work and research positioning are substantially reworked. V1 Table 1's comparison is replaced by v2 Table 18 with different works and criteria, emphasizing FedMSplit, client-side pre-training, and federated self-supervised learning. New contrastive-learning theory, DRO, and FedMOON references also support the revised discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. The main empirical-findings section becomes a short summary, while its detailed discussion, limitations, and existing appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a single-column layout, redraws Figures 1-2, moves empirical plots to the appendices, and combines replotted subsets into Figure 3 while retaining fuller appendix displays. The original pseudocode is reorganized into Algorithms 1-3, and several table structures and placements change.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, modular pseudocode, and new comparisons help, but v2 introduces an unsupported theoretical reformulation: Remark 1 claims a squared-distance objective equivalence, whereas Appendix G.1 only derives an unsquared-distance upper bound. Revised FedMAE main-table scores also conflict with retained appendix values, and resource-cost reporting is lost. These reduce rigor and transparency despite largely unchanged empirical evidence for the proposed method.
